title: Hardening inference-path entropy after scheduler optimization regression
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Following a schedule heuristic change deployed 2026-03-08, we observed a recurring runtime regression during capacity surges: kernel selection oscillation and suboptimal attention autotiling produced increased p95/p99 latency and a 22% throughput degradation for multi-sequence workloads. This ticket captures the incident follow-up, root cause investigation summary, and concrete hardening action items to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-03-08 02:12 UTC: Scheduler heuristic H2 (adaptive path probing) rolled out to canary cluster via runtime-1.24-canary.
2026-03-08 07:40 UTC: Autoscaling event triggered for east-us region; operator alert for elevated p99 latencies on several customer routes.
2026-03-08 08:05 UTC: On-call rotated and forced fallback to stable scheduler profile via emergency flag; partial recovery observed.
2026-03-09 14:30 UTC: Post-incident capture of traces, kernel-selection logs, and KV-cache hit/miss metrics.

2026-03-10 10:00 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis validated in lab: path probing introduced transient kernel affinity flips for medium-length sequences, causing KV-cache churn and attention autotiler to choose suboptimal tiles.
2026-03-11 16:20 UTC: Regression reproduced at 70% of original severity with synthetic loadbench and production-like traffic distributions.
2026-03-12 09:40 UTC: PR opened to add hysteresis to scheduler probing and KV-cache warmup guard (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4217).
root_cause: Scheduler adaptive probing (H2) introduced short-lived path switches when observed latency variance crossed a low threshold; the scheduler did not account for KV-cache warming cost, so a switch frequently chose a path that was locally optimal but globally regressional under load.
Attention autotiler heuristics assume stable kernel shapes; repeated kernel swaps exposed a poor autotile fallback that increased memory traffic and reduced fused-attention opportunities.
Existing canary signal aggregation window (30s) was too short to smooth out transient probe-induced variance, so the rollout amplified the regression rather than dampening it.
mitigations: Rolled back adaptive probing to conservative mode in all regions (2026-03-08 09:10 UTC) to restore baseline latency/throughput.
Enabled emergency KV-cache pinning for high-throughput routes to avoid cold-start churn during stabilization.
Added temporary rate limit on scheduler probing to limit path change frequency during autoscale events.
action_items: Add probe hysteresis and minimum-uptime requirement for new paths in scheduler (owner: Rajesh Patel) - due 2026-03-20 - estimate 3
Implement KV-cache warmup flag and API to pre-warm cache when switching kernel variants (owner: Leila Nguyen) - due 2026-03-27 - estimate 5
Improve autotiler fallback: prioritize fused-attention-compatible tiles when kernel churn detected (owner: Marco Rossi) - due 2026-04-03 - estimate 5
Extend canary signal aggregation window and add load-pattern-aware rollout gating (owner: Priya Shah) - due 2026-03-22 - estimate 2
Create an observability dashboard for path-switch correlation: kernel routes, KV-cache hit ratio, autotiler choices, and p95/p99 (owner: SRE Team) - due 2026-03-18 - estimate 2
Run targeted chaos test in staging that simulates autoscale spikes and forced kernel swaps; document thresholds that cause regression (owner: QA, contact: Daniel Kim) - due 2026-03-25 - estimate 3
Add automated regression test to CI that verifies no >10% throughput drop for representative multi-sequence workloads when toggling scheduler paths (owner: CI Team) - due 2026-03-29 - estimate 4

notes: This regression highlights an interaction class: scheduler-induced kernel churn -> KV-cache inefficiency -> autotiler degradation. The long-term fix combines scheduler conservative defaults, explicit cache warmup, and autotiler robustness. Prioritize low-risk mitigations first to avoid repeated incidents during rollouts.
